utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is the 24th of February. I would like to say hello to Mr. Stojic, Mr. Praljak, and I can see that Mr. Prlic, Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Coric are not here. So, of the three absent, two of them are not here because of ill health. I'd also like to pay tribute to the counsels and the other members here that are part of the Registrar and help us in the courtroom. I think Mr. Scott has something to say to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Mr. President, each of Your Honours, counsel. Your Honour, we are afraid it's the second day in the row but with the power outage this morning and the computers being down, Prosecution needs to ask to have until tomorrow to file its responses to the Defence exhibits tendered for Mr. Vegar. We'd ask to have until tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Yes, there was a problem with our electricity. I was supposed to start a hearing at half past 8 this morning, everything stopped. We took the accused back to the detention centre and all the hearings were cancelled. That will have consequence and of course we accept your request. Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours. First of all good afternoon. I rose in support of the Prosecution application and indeed to intimate that we may well be in a similar position. We were due to file today a response to the Prosecution's motion seeking to exclude what they describe as irrelevant evidence to be offered by our case, a motion they filed on the 19th of February. Because of the servers crashing, we've lost some time and it may well be that we ask that we be allowed to file tomorrow in a similar manner. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The same applies to you, Mr. Khan. Your dead-line is deferred to tomorrow. Let me ask Defence counsel for Mr. Prlic. Mr. Karnavas hasn't been here for several days. Is there any reason for his absence, because the main Defence counsels I expected to be here all the time unless there is some serious consideration to be looked at.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that it was common knowledge and I thought that Mr. Karnavas has informed the Chamber about that. He is in Cambodia this week, about discussing the provisional release of his client Iang Sary, and he is Defence counsel for Iang Sary at the Special Court in Cambodia. So he will be here next Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I didn't know that. I had heard that he had gone abroad and lately I saw Mr. Khan in Cambodia on TV, but I didn't know that for Mr. Karnavas was there too. We look forward to his return next week. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I just ask the question, I take it Mr. Prlic is informed of this state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course Mr. Karnavas, before he agreed to be Defence counsel for Iang Sary who asked for Mr. Karnavas specifically, he first consulted Mr. Prlic and then with the Registrar of the Tribunal as well. So he was granted permission both by the Registrar and by Dr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Actually my question was much narrower. Mr. Prlic is aware that now he is not in the courtroom and his lead counsel also is not in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I am in contact with Dr. Prlic every day and he is kept abreast of all the proceedings in detail in the courtroom, and he said that if I were present, then he would be fine with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. This was not a question of distrust. I'm not surprised at all by your answer, but it is our duty to see to it that these things go fine. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everybody inside and outside the courtroom. And, Mr. Pinjuh, good afternoon to you too. Sir, I'd like to focus at the beginning today once again on the Decree on the Armed Forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And for this purpose I'd like you to turn, and this is in the 2D Defence binder, to document 2D 00588. 2D 00588.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but maybe I could be of assistance to my learned friend. Is he sure of the number? Is it 2D? If you are talking about the Decree on the Armed Forces, it should be a P document. P 588.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: My apology. That's indeed incorrect. P 00588. Apologies to everyone for the confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, you have the document in front of you now. Now, sir, this document, this is the version that was adopted by the HVO HZ-HB on 17 October 1992. You see that in the heading of the document; is that correct? It's right at the top, it says: "Decree on the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna Armed Forces was changed and amended at the session of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna presidency of 17 October 1992."

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, this edited version follows upon the previous version which you also had the opportunity to look at yesterday, and that was P 00587. We are only going to focus on this version today, but the questions that I'm asking would be equally applicable to that earlier version because the provisions we are referring to are identical in both versions. The first thing I'd like you to look at is Article 2. And you see that Article 2 starts off with: "The HZ-HB defence system is a unified form of organisation of armed forces, administrative bodies and legal entities with the purpose of ensuring timely and organised prevention of attacks and other dangers confronting the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." So, sir, this being -- the HZ-HB system being a unit -- or defence system being a unified form of organisation, that means that the whole defence system is comprised of many units, each one forming a little cog in a larger defence machine; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And the defence office in Citluk of which you were the head, would then also be a little cog in this big machine?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it says that the unified system consists of armed forces administrative bodies. Let's focus on administrative bodies for a moment. If we look at Article 10 of the decree. Can you turn to Article 10. Right beneath Article 10 it says, "The HZ-HB administrative bodies are as follows," and then it starts off with the Defence Department. So stating the obvious, the Defence Department of the HZ-HB is seen as -- or sorry, of the HVO is seen as an administrative body; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Then let's turn to Article 12. It says -- and this is still under the heading of administrative bodies, it says: "Defence tasks as described under Article 10, item 1, of this decree shall be entrusted to defence administrations and defence offices established within the Defence Department." So in other words, defence administrations and defence offices, they are part of the Defence Department; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And in the performance of your functions, therefore, you were not in competition with the Defence Department but you were actually part of the Defence Department; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And, sir, if we take that a step further perhaps, if we look at all the other little cogs of this machine and including municipal HVO organisations, they would also be part of this whole system, not in competition with the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain that, what organs did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I was thinking of municipal HVOs. The municipal HVO in Citluk, for instance, which you referred to yesterday, that would also be part of this whole defence -- unified defence system?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And the Citluk HVO would not be in competition with the Department of Defence in defence matters?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really have to object here. I think the question is too broad and I don't think such a broad question is useful to us if the witness has to speculate. So could we have a better definition of what is actually wanted because these questions related to general organisation, we are going to have a witness about that, but I think that it would be better if the Prosecutor were to specify and say which areas the Citluk HVO would have been in competition with the Defence Department or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, if there is a need, the Chamber will interrupt the OTP and if we don't do that, it seem that is we understand what he is saying. So please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Pinjuh, would you agree that the Citluk HVO would not be in competition in defence matters with the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and answer that in the best way possible as I understood the question. The HVO of Citluk municipality had its civilian section which related to the municipal assembly, as it was called previously, and it had its HVO Main Staff which worked exclusively on matters which you are in fact asking me about, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. The point, sir, is that all the organs of the HVO in defence matters were playing on the same team and working towards the same goal; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: One more aspect on this concerning municipalities. If we look at the heading of this decree and it says at the top, second paragraph basically, "Pursuant" -- just above where it says decree: "Pursuant to Article 7 of the decision on establishing the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Narodni List 1 of 92, the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna issued the following." Then follows the decree. Now, sir, do you know what the presidency or who the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was or how it was constituted?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know that. It would be pure speculation on my part if I were to hazard an answer. Perhaps I do know some names, and I do recollect some, but I don't really know who was elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I'm not talking about specific individual people, but who were these people? They were representatives of the municipalities constituting the territory of the HZ-HB, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, yesterday -- let's move on to something else. Yesterday you stated that as far as mobilisation is concerned, mobilisation was the preserve of Mate Boban. He was the only one to declare mobilisation and on 1 June 1992, we looked at the order that he issued, and basically in para-phrasing your further evidence, this single order served as a one-time continual order for mobilisation throughout the rest of 1992 and 1993. Do you recall that evidence of yours?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Just for the record, the document we are referring to, and we don't need to look at it now, was 2D 01364.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like you to have a look at Article 9 of this decree. Article 9 of the decree says: "The Croatian Defence Council shall," and then if we go down to point 6, "decide on conducting mobilisation." So, sir, if we look at this decree which comes from October 1992, your statement on mobilisation being the preserve of Mate Boban exclusively is not quite accurate, is it?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by what I said earlier. I'm not a lawyer myself, but it says here "shall decide about conducting," that is to say, how to implement mobilisation. That's what it says, who does what. That's how I understand this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's look at Article 38. Article 38: "Persons responsible for preparation and execution of mobilisation of the armed forces shall be," and then 1: "The head of the Defence Department preparation and execution of mobilisation of the armed forces." So we see that the head of the Defence Department, which was at that stage Mr. Bruno Stojic, he had a very important role to play regarding mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since the Defence Department is a professional body and a body of management and organisation then it would be logical that these two bodies actually implement this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then once again harking back to Article 2, because this is all part of a unified defence system, all these little organisations or all these bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's look briefly at Article 12 again. Article 12 states: "Defence tasks," and this deals with the defence administrations and defence offices. "Defence tasks as described under Article 10, item 1, shall be entrusted to the defence administrations and defence offices established within the Defence Department." So, sir, is it correct that you took your instructions, you, as a member of a defence office, took your instructions from the Defence Department ultimately? Or they came from there?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I received instructions and orders from the chief of the department above me that was responsible for defence, the immediate superior department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Would that be the Mostar defence administration?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And they would receive their instructions from the Department of Defence itself?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could put it that way, although, the administration has under its responsibility tasks and frameworks of work in cooperation with the territorial commands and administrations within the Defence Department. First of all, I mean this administration for organisational matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And in regard to that, let's look at the very final paragraph of Article 10 of this decree: "The head of the Defence Department issues regulations pertaining to his authority and technical instructions for conducting affairs as defined under items 1 and 2 of this article." You see that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: So are you aware of instructions or regulations by Mr. Stojic regarding how Article 10(1) would be implemented?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that I didn't understand your question. Could you put it in more precise terms. What sort of instructions are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the specific mechanics of implementing Article 10(1). Do you know whether Mr. Stojic issued any instructions or regulations, guide-lines? How Article 10(1) would be implemented. Chains of command, reporting structures, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, is it safe to say that ultimately your superior at the very top of this defence structure would have been Mr. Stojic? I'm talking about you personally.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the Defence Department, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, something interesting, if we look at Article 10(1), it says, the Defence Department, it's work is related to "monitoring and coordinating activities aimed at achieving the agreed policy of the defence system." What is this agreed policy which is being referred to? What would that refer to? Who would set it? If you know.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this has to do with the mobilisation plan which was worked out based on assessments made by the territorial commands and the Main Staff while the department for mobilisation affairs after receiving the same kind of plan for the maintenance of manpower levels of the units based on assessments of the threat and the possibilities of mobilisation, they developed a mobilisation plan which would include, first of all, a numerical framework, and this was the work and the tasks I was interested in as the chief of the defence office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: We are going to come back to this aspect later, and I would like you to just remember our discussion now because we will be seeing some other bodies which were also setting policy, perhaps, which was implemented in this way. But before we go there let's look at a few other provisions. If we could just quickly turn to Article 11, just the next article. And this is still within the section dealing with administrative bodies. It says: "The General Staff shall be founded within the Defence Department in order to carry out tasks prescribed" -- or "described under Article 10, paragraph 2 ..." So, sir, is it correct that the General Staff, or the Main Staff as it is also referred to, of the HVO, is part of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and in my previous reply I said it was they who made the assessment of the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. So the Main Staff would also be ultimately subordinate to Mr. Stojic as the head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was part of the Defence Department but in some of the articles you can see also that they are responsible directly to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Sir, now, just we've been dealing with administrative matters. Before stepping off this document, let's turn to Article 30 of the document. And now we've stepped off from the section dealing with administrative matters or organs, and we are now dealing with leading and commanding the armed forces, which you will see just written above Article 29. But looking at Article 30, it says, second paragraph: "The Supreme Command of the armed forces may delegate certain tasks of leading and commanding the armed forces to the head of the Defence Department." So, sir, from this you will agree that the functions and powers of the head of the Defence Department, and that was Mr. Stojic at the time, was not only limited to administrative affairs, he could also, if such powers were delegated to him, command the army and issue commands and orders, or lead the army?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say what exactly Mr. Boban delegated to whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But in terms of this, it was possible?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's highly unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, if we look at all these provisions that we've dealt with so far in this decree, it seems that the head of the Defence Department features quite prominently in the whole defence setup envisaged in this decree. Would you agree that Bruno Stojic as the head of the Defence Department was key to the functioning of the defence system in the HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the function of head is a very important one, regardless of what name is attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let's step off this decree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. I've been listening both to your questions and to the responses. When you say to the witness, for example, that Mr. Stojic plays a key role in the functioning of the defence system, are you insinuating that he is also involved in military operations, because Mr. Kruger, I don't know if you were in the army, but when you talk about the defence system there are several components. You have the civilian component, you have the mobilisation component, and you have the administrative component, and also the operational components. When you asked your question a moment ago, were you including that the supreme commander, Mr. Boban, could delegate to the head of the Defence Department, that is Mr. Stojic, certain powers in terms of operational matters? That's the question that comes to mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I was putting the proposition to the witness more in a general sense to gauge his reaction. In the context of his answers, the focus was mainly on the administrative functions of Mr. Boban -- Mr. Stojic in light of that the witness had said that he was not aware of any powers being delegated, if any, by Mr. Boban. So I wasn't particularly focused on that aspect in my question. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I didn't want to intervene before my learned friend had completed his examination concerning this decree, but I would like to read out Article 10(1)(1) because my learned friend was asking about establishing policy. I think that this article clearly states what sort of policy is referred to, so as to avoid misunderstanding it says here: "... Following and harmonizing activities in implementing the established policy of the defence system." So from Article 1 it does not follow that the Defence Department actually established the policy, but it only followed and harmonised activities in the implementation of a policy that had already been established. This is a policy of the defence system, not any other kind of policy. I felt I had to read this out because I thought that inadvertently things had been taken out of context and might be misunderstood. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, I wanted to ask you a question but I was waiting for Mr. Kruger to finish. You, in fact, worked under the control of the Defence Department, we all know that, that's not the issue here. But as regards the policy of the Defence Department, to your knowledge, and perhaps you don't know the answer to this question, but according to your knowledge, was it Mr. Boban who defined the policy and then the Defence Department simply implemented the policy; or according to your knowledge again, was it Mr. Stojic who defined the policy and then you implemented it? What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't really answer questions about any sort of policy because I am afraid of what it might imply. All I can talk about is the implementation of the tasks assigned to my office by the superior administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand correctly, as regarding the policy and the definition of the policy, you really don't know who decided on the policy? You implemented the policy, if I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we can now turn to the Prosecution binder, which is the binder on the table next to you, to look at a series of documents. Yes, that one. I'd like to go through a number of documents signed or authored by Mr. Stojic, with you. And the first one is Exhibit P 00517. P 00517. Now, sir, this is a command on 22 September 1992, by Bruno Stojic as head of the Defence Department to the OS Mostar, Siroki Brijeg, the HVO Main Staff, and the operational zone south-east Herzegovina. And if we look at this command, we see it says: Number 1: "Establish sector of Mostar as an operations group," et cetera. Number 2: "From existing battalions of the Mostar municipal office form two reserve battalions." Number 3: "Mostar municipality staff to be transformed into a command of Mostar sector." Number 5, if you look at that: "Siroki Brijeg municipal staff to form a independent battalion and mixed artillery battalion." And so it goes on. Now, sir, my first question on this is: You would agree that this is an order going to the operations of the HVO military? Constituting military organs?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really don't see in the document be -- I do have to object. What operations? It mentions the system here, the organisation, so if operations are mentioned, this is a trap for the witness. The word "operation" is being used in a very too facile manner. It says here organisation, not operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't think that Mr. Kruger is setting a trap. We've known him for many years and he is not the kind of person who would set a trap for the witness. Let him ask his questions and the Judges will intervene if need be in order to make things more precise. Mr. Kruger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Also for the trust placed in me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, this command --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, I trust everyone. I trust the Defence counsel, I trust the OTP, and when a witness has been sworn in, I trust the witness as well. I trust everyone. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, this command, it seems to be quite an important command going to certain structures and creation of certain units. Now, the first thing to notice from this order is, do you notice that there is no indication in terms of which legislation or legal authority Mr. Stojic is issuing this order? You agree? There is nothing.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: There's no provision in this order or command stating in terms of section or article so and so of this law or that decree I order, there's nothing like that; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is, if I remember correctly. It could fall under point 8 in the Decree on Armed Forces. This concerns re-organisation and I see it's addressed to the municipal staff of Mostar and Siroki Brijeg, the Main Staff which will carry out this reorganisation and municipal staffs are being abolished, so all this fell under the purview of Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. But there's nothing in the document saying referring to those provisions?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, I'm not a lawyer but I can agree that it doesn't say here pursuant to article such and such and so on, but everything else is as I said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And sir, it's also so that there is no indication in this document that Mr. Stojic was acting on the advice or pursuant to somebody else's decision?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't see that from this order. It must be in some other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Mr. Kruger is dealing with a very complicated matter that I'm endeavouring to understand in relationship to paragraph 9. Based on what we can understand, and Mr. Kruger is quite right to indicate that this text mentions no particular other text, and you've just recognised that yourself, but can't we say here that there is a document that says that in September of 1992, the HVO decided to put all of the units into the Main Staff of the HVO, that is all of the municipalities that came thus far under the Territorial Defence, which enables us to better understand paragraph 9 which it states that is all of the existing seals because we know because we have examined all of the JNA documents and all of the BiH and HVO documentation, we know that this issue of the seals is a very important one. And here, under 9, it states that the existing seals of the municipal staff shall be used as official seals until new ones are made. So doesn't this document in fact state that the military component of HVO grants -- has full authority over all of the units that come under the municipalities? Can you confirm what I've just said, or on the contrary, perhaps my understanding is wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that this concerned re-organisation of all combat units and the municipal staff ceases to exist pursuant to this decision. The units remain and above them are the zones of operations and the Main Staff. So this is a re-organisation, probably the same people from these staffs who were sent to the zones of operations to the higher commands or some of them became reservists until needed by the wartime units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, the point I -- the final question I have on this document is, the signature of Mr. Bruno Stojic as head of the Defence Department, and the stamp of the Defence Department, that would be sufficient for people receiving this command to implement it?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It ought to be implemented by those to whom it is addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And they'd recognise -- they would recognise the authority of Mr. Stojic; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to these units, there is a route through which an excerpt from the order is supposed to reach them. From the Main Staff an excerpt of the order is forwarded down to the line to those it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid things are becoming a bit confused. You have said that the municipal units were seized by the Main Staff, what Main Staff are you talking about, the municipal Main Staff or the HVO Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Main Staff of the HVO. The municipal staffs are being abolished by this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you please take a look at who this document is being sent to. I'd like to try to understand this with you. Mr. Stojic has sent this document to the municipal staff of Mostar, to the OS of Siroki Brijeg, to the HVO Main Staff, and to the operational zones of the south-east of Herzegovina, which this seems to mean that this document is being sent directly to the municipal Main Staff and it does not go through the HVO Main Staff. What can you say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the HVO Main Staff mentioned here. I cannot comment on whether they went directly, whether they were sent directly or through the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S version we can see that there are a series of dashes and a list, OS Mostar, OS Siroki Brijeg, GS HVO, and OZJ/I Herzegovina. So there are four bodies that are receiving this order, and I believe that this is the original that in fact was sent to Siroki Brijeg and that's why OS Siroki Brijeg is underlined, and as proof, if you take a look at the stamp, the document has been registered in Siroki Brijeg. I'm not a member of the HVO military, but I'm trying to understand the document.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that the municipal assembly of Siroki Brijeg, the municipal staff of Territorial Defence are mentioned here. This might be for their information, but the implementation of the order will be done by the units it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let's turn to document P 00779. It's in the same binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, this document is an order by Bruno Stojic of 19 November 1992, and if we see the order, it says: "All units of the HVO, especially the military police, must ensure free passage without any hold-ups of the special-purpose unit that will be moving along the Mostar-Travnik route. I hereby order all members of the HVO on this route to be ready to provide any kind of assistance to the members of the special-purpose unit." Now, once again there's no indication which power -- under which power Mr. Stojic is ordering this; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this order before, so I can't really comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But, sir, if you had received an order like this from Mr. Stojic, would you have executed such an order?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the head of an office and here it says "unit" so I couldn't have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: You have no reason to think that an order like this would not be honoured by the units it is addressed to, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, interesting, you will agree that the order contained here is for specific action by units. So this is not merely an administrative command or order, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. No mention is made of any action here. It's just some route that is mentioned, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, it says, "I hereby order all members of the HVO to ensure" and especially the military police, "they must ensure free passage without any hold-ups." That's certainly an order to act in a particular way, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said that I really can't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that this document, if we need to think about what provision or under what legal authority Mr. Stojic is acting, this is an ideal example of perhaps where he is acting under Article 30 of the Decree of Armed Forces, exercising command delegated by Mr. Stojic -- by Mr. Boban, isn't that possible?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that because command and control is something that the Main Staff does. It's their authority to do that and the lowerly [as interpreted] units too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, finally on this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I, like you, am looking at this document that has been issued by Mr. Stojic, that is not disputed, and the registration number is 02 for the Department of Defence, and then number 1 that shows Mr. -- it's Mr. Stojic who, in 1992, drafted 210 documents of various types. It comes from Mostar, 19th of November, 1993, and he is asking all the HVO units, in particular the military police, to allow free passage and there seems to be a special unit that is going to be travelling on the road from Mostar to Travnik. What is this special unit, according to you? Perhaps you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We don't know. Okay. Mr. Kruger, the witness doesn't know what this special unit is. Perhaps this order concerns some particular unit, but we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, I do have one more question on this document, and this doesn't concern whether this document is accurate or not. It says: "All units of the HVO, especially the military police, must ensure..." To your knowledge, isn't it correct that Mr. Stojic also could issue orders or exert authority over the military police?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, let's turn to P 00875. P 00875. Now, sir, this is a document dated 15 January 1993, and it was issued by Mr. Bruno Stojic. Sorry, sorry, I turned too far, Your Honour. My apologies. This is a 7 December 1992 order issued by Bruno Stojic, Slobodan Praljak, and Valentin Coric. And this order deals with checkpoints, military checkpoints. It states: "Based on the order by General Slobodan Praljak and the head of the Department of Defence, Bruno Stojic, stipulating the appearance of checkpoints of the military police of the HVO, insignia on checkpoints and of military police officers as well as the procedure in conducting control at the checkpoints, we hereby issue a common order." And then follows what is in essence is a set of regulations and instructions on how to proceed and how to conduct military checkpoints. My first question to you is, do you know whether this order was also received within Citluk?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, once again with regard to Mr. Stojic, will you agree, as there is no indication of what legal provision he is exercising his authority under, his authority is recognized by the people who received this order, and they would implement this order or recognise his authority then? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What this is about is what the soldiers looked like mostly. In this case a military policeman, what he should look like, how he should behave, and we know that in the Defence Department there is a security department too, where there is a military police administration, so I see nothing to be challenged here, and in the signatures too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. But I think you don't disagree that Mr. Stojic has clear authority to issue an instruction or an order like this, but let's turn to Mr. Praljak. Based on what authority would he be able to issue this command, to your mind?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't answer a question like that because it's at a level above me. It's beyond me. So if you could ask me something linked to my job and the work I did at the time, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, in November 1992, if you received an order from General Praljak, would you have obeyed that order or carried out that order?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say now. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Were you aware that General Praljak was performing certain functions, defence functions within the HZ-HB during 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present in the defence of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Now, what posts he occupied, what functions he had, I really don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, when the General Praljak will testify I can always present this document to him and ask him questions, but let me ask you a question now. Is it normal, in the documents that you laid your eyes on at the time, was it normal to see General Praljak signing but no stamp appears? Is that normal procedure? General Praljak, when you testify, you will be able to answer that, so let's not lose any more time. Let me take up this document and put it into my own file and I will present it to you when the time comes. Very well. Witness, could you answer my question. Was it normal practice for somebody to sign the document, but not affix a stamp to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, I told you -- THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] No, I'm not going to answer, Your Honour. All I wanted to say is that the previous document, you can take that aside, too, and put in your file to ask me subsequently. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's move on then to document P 01140, which is just the next document. Now, sir, this document is dated 15 January 1993. It's an order by Mr. Bruno Stojic as head of the Defence Department, and it is sent to the Main Staff, and the minister of defence of BH, military police administration and files. This document is basically an order which is to the Main Staff of the armed forces of the HVO. They shall "immediately establish direct contact with all operation zones and commands of the army of BiH, or BH, in the territory of provinces 3, 8, 10, and 1, 5, and 9, in order to make the decision of the HVO of 15 January" -- sorry, "the decision of the HVO HZ-HB of 15 January, specific for its implementation". And what this order basically says is all units within the territories -- or within provinces 3, 8, and 10 must subordinate themselves to the HVO, and all units in the other provinces have to subordinate themselves of course to the ABiH. Goes on to say that those units which do not subordinate themselves to the HVO will then be seen as para-military formations. Now, sir, first of all, this order must have been received in Citluk as well for implementation, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just looked at this document hastily and I don't see any reason why Citluk should have received it, nor have I ever seen this document before. And if you look at who it was addressed to on the back, then you can see that there was absolutely no chance that this document could have reached Citluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, maybe not this document, but at any stage were you aware of -- sorry, let me ask you a different question. Apart from -- or were there any HVO units stationed on the territory of Citluk?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Were there any units from any other military organisation, the ABiH, for instance, stationed in Citluk or on the territory of Citluk?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the HVO units, as far as I remember, there were a couple of members who were Muslims who later, as far as I know, joined the BH Army, but there were never any BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. So we've established that this order would not have applied to Citluk then, probably. But I'm still interested in one aspect of this order. Now, it says that this order is pursuant to a decision of the HVO HZ-HB of 15 January 1993. Do you know who the HVO HZ-HB was, or what body that was?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council was the assembly or parliament of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But this specific body here, isn't that the body which was headed by or chaired by Mr. Jadranko Prlic and on which the heads of the various Departments of Defence, of Finance, of Internal Affairs, sat and that they took decisions?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't speak about the composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Well, sir, regardless then of whom this body was which is being referred to, if you think back to Article 10(1) of the Decree of the Armed Forces, I flagged to you that we'd come back to this, we don't need to go to it, but Article 10(1). Do you remember it said that the Department of Defence performs work related to, then 1, monitoring and coordinating activities aimed at achieving the agreed policy of the defence system. Would you agree, sir, that this decision by the HVO HZ-HB would seem to fall right in that, a policy decision which is now to be implemented by the Defence Department and within the defence system?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I am stepping on to a new document, perhaps this would be a time to take the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are quite right. Yes, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to take advantage of this opportunity to apologise to my learned friend Mr. Kruger if my previous comment was understood as his intention to impute something or to interpret something falsely to the witness. Now, I have great sympathies for my colleague Mr. Kruger, I know that he would never do that, and has never done that, but I think that sometimes unintentionally some mistakes might be made, and as I always react temperamentally, then this was one such case. There was a mistake that was made when the document was shown, P 1140, that document, on page 26 in line 16 to 17 with the addressees -- where the addressees were mentioned who received this order, I think it was through pure oversight that my colleague Mr. Kruger omitted to say the staff of the BH Army which was also supposed to receive this decision and was one of the addressees. I think that that is fairly important, because when we look at all the people and instances who received the order then we can understand the order in a proper light, so I apologise to my colleague. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And it is indeed so addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you Mr. Kruger. Right. We shall now have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, we don't have much time left. I'm going to show you five more documents. Now, the first one I'm going to call on your experience from 1994 onwards as the head of the personnel administration in the Department of Defence. And I'd like to show you a document and get your comments on that, and the document is P 10336. 10336. Now, sir, this document is by Mr. Bruno Stojic. It's dated the 10th of March, and you'll see that it's addressed to Mr. Gojko Susak personally at the Ministry of Defence Republic of Croatia. He says herein: "Please find attached the proposal for Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic to be given a rank in the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia and the supplementary proposal to be given a rank of higher officer in the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia." Now, sir, my first question is: Mr. Stojic is directing this request to the minister of foreign affairs of another country, the Republic of Croatia. In your experience, what standing would Mr. Stojic have to issue such a request?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment to make on this. As I said, this is a level far above the level at which I was, so I'm really unable to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let's then look at the practicalities of the document. If you turn the page, you will see on the next page -- sorry, for you it would be the next page after that, the one you are looking at. This is the page which has a whole series of points on it saying recommendation for rank in the OSRH, armed forces of the Republic of Croatia. And then it says number 1, commission; 2, promotion; 3, posting. Sir, if you could turn one ... Yes, I think you now have the correct page. Now, sir, this contains information on General Petkovic's career. And if you look at point 9, it says date of leaving the JNA, or the Yugoslav Army, was 25 July 1991. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And point 10, it says the date of joining the HV, or the Croatian army, was the very next day, 26 July 1991. You see that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: If we go down to point 17, it says, length of service before joining the HV, that was 19 years. You see that, too?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And then it says years of pensionable service is 21 years. So if we make the sum from 25 July 1991, General Petkovic had 19 years' service, and after that you add two more years' service, that brings you to 1993, and if we look at the date of this letter, this is 10 March 1993. So, sir, my question to you is: From this would you agree or does it appear, at least, that in March 1993 General Petkovic was still in the employ of the HV, or was still accumulating pensionable service in the HV?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question. As pensionable service, I think that it's calculated differently in the army. In the army they have an accelerated pension plan which might be the reason for these numbers, so military pensionable service is calculated as being longer than the actual time served.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That helps, and we can step off that point. There's another interesting point that I'd like to look at, and that is if you go two pages further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you haven't finished, I will let you finish before I intervene. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: If we can go to the page starting with "28, Statement of Reasons." This is reasons based on which the mentioned proposal was presented. Do you have that page?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, item 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: That's right. And this is signed by Bruno Stojic at the bottom; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, this being a proposal to the Croatian army or at least this is to convince the Croatian army or authorities in the Republic of Croatia to give General Petkovic a rank, it says, paragraph 1: "From the political perspective, Mr. Petkovic has a clearly defined opinion and he puts into practice, with an absolute consistency, the general Croatian political conception as well as specific conception regarding circumstances in Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, sir, this is by -- a letter by Bruno Stojic. He is the minister -- or well, head of the Department of Defence of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. He is writing this letter to the minister of defence of the Republic of Croatia, another country. So if there is reference to putting into practice the general Croatian political conception, which Croatian political conception is this, the one of the Republic of Croatia, or the one of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see here what there is for me to comment on. It says what it says. I really have no comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I didn't see you. I was reading the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wish to assist pursuant to instructions by His Honour Judge Antonetti when there is a discrepancy between the original and the translation. I think it should be pointed out that in the original Croatian document when it says carry out the general Croatian political conception, Croatian is not written with a capital letter. And it is therefore an adjective which does not refer to the state policy of the Republic of Croatia or to any policy of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which might exist, but to Croatian policy in general terms which might refer to Croats in Canada, in the USA or anywhere else. In the English text, this word is capitalized, it has a capital C, which I think does not correspond to its meaning. For this reason, the witness is probably unable to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger, I imagine you've heard that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you to my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, I would still like to ask you what was your understanding in the last sentence when there is reference to, as well as specific conception regarding circumstances in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is now in reference to the political -- the general Croatian political conception in general. What does that mean, putting that in place with regard to the circumstances in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to the territorial part where the Croatian corpus is. That's all, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Why would it be important for the Republic of Croatia to hear that somebody, which they are going to give a rank in their army, implements or is good at implementing a general Croat conception or a general Croatian political conception?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a highly generalised expression. It would be the same if they were contemplating a lower officer's rank, but it's very difficult for me to comment on the correspondence between two states. This is way above my head. Please bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, let's have a look at Exhibit P 04646. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have three questions on this document. First of all, I'm not absolutely certain that you are the most appropriate witness to answer these questions but let's set that aside. In the very first document, which dealt with Mr. Petkovic's CV, we know he was born October 11th, 1949, in Sibenik, that he joined the Croatian army on July 26th, 1991. And I can see under column 8 the question, Did he sign a contract and the answer is yes. What exactly does that mean for you, did he sign a contract with the HVO? And then, it states that it's a two-year contract. What do you have to say to that? If you can't answer, just say, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the next page, amongst the reasons for granting the promotion to General Petkovic, I see something under paragraph 4, it states the following: The major portion of the HZ and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was defended under General Petkovic. Does that mean that General Petkovic defended also the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that's what's written here, it seems to me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with this formulation and we have already mentioned who it was that committed aggression not only against Bosnia-Herzegovina, but against all the other peoples as well. So it's quite clear that defending part of the territory they are defending the entire state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps a bit like Sherlock Holmes we will be able to clarify a mystery. Please look at the various posts, the various jobs that General Petkovic has occupied. He was the deputy to the commander of the 113th Brigade of the Croatian army, he commanded the 130th Brigade, and then he was the chief of artillery in Split, in the OZ of Split, and then he was the head of training operations in the OZ in Split as of -- from January 21st to the 14th of April, 1992. And it seems that he also became the Main Staff head in June of 1992. Have I -- is that exactly what it written here, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means, then, that General Petkovic joined the HVO on April 14th. Please turn the page again. And if you look at the end, this document is signed by Mr. Stojic. The document is dated Mostar, March 10th. In other words, a month before that. How can you explain this mystery? Well, because on March 10th, General Petkovic was in Split. He wasn't in Mostar, well, at least apparently.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we may draw your attention to the years. The document signed by Mr. Stojic was dated 1993, whereas General Petkovic was appointed the Chief of the Main Staff in June 1992, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree with what counsel has just said. We have a stamp and a signature. Mr. Stojic signed the document. I have my glasses on so I can see, and it says Mostar, March 10th. Well, there was a 2 and there's been a handwritten 3, it was corrected by hand. It's strange.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please look at the original document in the Croatian language and also look at the first page of this document, and then it will be quite clear that this is a document from March 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Well, for the purposes of the transcript, under the reasons -- in fact we have two documents. There were two B/C/S documents translated into English. The first document -- and I agree with what was said a moment ago. There is a 3 written over the 2, but there's another document which is almost identical and the date is 1992. There is no 3 there. Perhaps the document was indeed originated in 1993, that is possible. Of course, Witness, you can't say much about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also see the number 3 here above the 2, and I think that what one can see here is logical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It must be the secretary who mistyped or who typed or perhaps used a pre-prepared form and in this pre-prepared form the date was 1992, that could been explanation, and they didn't pay attention to the fact that the date was incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the fact that you are quite familiar with the Croatian language now, could you please look at the Croatian document where you can see there is a marking shown that the document was sent by telefax, and you will see that the pages were sent in March, the 10th of March, 1993. So I think that resolves the dilemma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The facts states 18 hours 24. 1823.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm still a bit puzzled and I put it into the record, rather, that I expect, really, the witness to have an explanation, although one never knows. I am struck by the fact that we have the last document twice, and the body of the text seems to be identical. I see no difference in any way. However, the first one has an ingress Oslobodjenje; the second does not have this. The first has an extra line at the bottom where the commander of the OZ would be expected to sign, but there is no such signature. The second one does not have the title, and it does not have this last line but, nevertheless, it is also signed apparently by Mr. Stojic. If one looks at the stamps, one can see that the stamps are at different places, and also the signature is not identical. I wonder, Mr. Pinjuh, can you give an explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not disappointed. I can understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, it was a minor detail. It's not fundamental. Mr. Kruger, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, if we can turn to document P 04646. And I'm going to show you two documents directly after each other which are very similar. Now, sir, you have the document, it's dated the 30th of August, 1993. It's addressed to Major-General Slobodan Praljak, and it's written and signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic. And in the English translation it says this is an "Invitation to a meeting of the collegium of the heads of Department of Defence which will be held," et cetera. Now, if you can hold your finger in at that point and just turn two documents further to document P 05045. Now, for the record, the original B/C/S versions of these two documents have virtually identical wordings but the English translation of this one, which is a letter of 14 September to -- 1993, to Major-General Slobodan Praljak from Mr. Bruno Stojic. It says this is a summons. "You are hereby summoned to a session of the collegium of the president of the Defence Department, which will be convened," et cetera, et cetera. Now, sir, from your experience of these matters, could you perhaps help us in understanding this letter, is it a summons or is it an invitation? These two letters.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand this as an invitation because I see it was sent from the office of the president. In wartime the president has his office consisting of the head, the chief of the Main Staff, and people proposed by them and appointed by the president, so that's how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Kruger, I think we should ask the interpreters to give their interpretation of the word "poziv" which figures both times.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: That "poziv" can mean either summons or invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you to the interpreters. Now, let's try and clear this up and let's look at another document, and this document is P 04756. P 04756.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would not intervene for the translation because Ms. Nozica said that she would go back, but, anyway, it may go to very complicated questions. In line 23, on page 38, when we discuss the document which was on table, the translation said it was sent from the office of the president. It is quite wrong. It was sent from office of the "predstojnik" [phoen], meaning head of the office. Thank you. And pardon me, and the witness said exactly the same word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to come in here because I was somewhat lost. I thought that it was the office of the president and I was thinking in terms of Mr. Boban, but then I see that the meeting is a meeting of the collegium of the Department of Defence. Now, the office of this president, and the signature is President Bruno Stojic, was Mr. Stojic president of that collegium? I'm talking about the collegium.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say he was the president of the collegium. I think the members held the same rank. All the members of the collegium were of equal rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are you serious, Mr. Pinjuh? We have a head of department and we have his subordinates and the head of department cannot be of the same rank as his subordinate chiefs of administration, can he? I'm sorry, Ms. Alaburic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think there's a huge misunderstanding here caused by interpretation. The witness is talking about the council of the president of Herceg-Bosna which is why I think he said that this was a body in which the members were more or less of the same rank. However, the interpretation seems to be that this is the collegium of the head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I refrained up to now in view of His Honour Judge Antonetti's intervention today who said that we should not be hasty with objections and that we should trust the Court. However, something is happening here now. The witness has said at least three time that this was a very high level far above his head and that he didn't know how all this functioned. If we are showing the witness documents without any sort of introduction, without asking the witness whether he knew that there was a collegium, whether he knew who its members were, there will certainly be this sort of confusion. The witness himself said, quite unprovoked, I was at the follow level, I'm really not aware of all this. So a document is being put to the witness that the witness knows nothing about, and that's the source of the confusion. We are just wasting time here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Ms. Nozica has just reminded us of something very important. As Judges, we have learned that on occasions in the Department of Defence there were meetings between the various departments, Mr. Stojic, and this was referred to as the collegium. That's one thing. And we also are aware of the fact that the president, Mr. Boban, brought together people as well. We have a document before us now. The question I ask is whether this document relates to the meetings at the level of the Department of Defence or else at the level of Mr. Boban. Ms. Nozica has just reminded us quite rightly that at your level you are not really cognizant with these matters, so if you are not just answer, Well, I don't know, and Mr. Kruger will go on to a different question. What do you say, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot comment on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not going to ask you to comment on the document, but as a matter of the problem we have with the interpretation of the B/C/S word "poziv," which can mean invitation or it can mean a summons, I'd like to show you this document, which is P 4756, and just ask you whether that would change your assessment that "poziv" means invitation. And what this is, these are the minutes of the heads of Defence Department meeting held on 2 September 1993. Now, for your background or information, the first document that I showed you, that was P 04646, which said invitation to General Praljak to attend a meeting on the 1st of September. If I'm not mistaken that meeting was then held on the 2nd of September, so these are the minutes of that meeting. And if we look in the very first paragraph, the second sentence, it says: "The deputy chief of the HVO Main Staff sat in for the commander of the HVO Main Staff. The head of the Department of Defence," which is Mr. Stojic, "emphasised that in future the commander of the HVO Main Staff should attend every board meeting." Meaning that -- or do you think or does this affects your interpretation? Isn't the interpretation to be attached to "poziv" that it's actually a binding summons?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on this either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, if we can step on to another matter, and I'm now going to jump to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I get the impression that Mr. Kruger is mixing up apples and pears. Look at the last document not the translation of "poziv" -- well, the first paragraph to me seems to indicate that the collegium of the Department of Defence met on the 1st of September, 1993, at 9 a.m., in the office of the head of the department, and there was an agenda. There was an agenda. So is this -- this is the collegium of the Department of Defence, not the collegium of Mr. Boban. Do you agree that the minutes refer to discussions that took place at the Department of Defence, not with Mr. Boban since right in the first paragraph you can see that the meeting took place on the 1st September in the offices of the head of the department. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me come back to the word "poziv," to establish whether it's a invitation or a summons. I assume that Mr. Boban convenes meetings. He is president so he convenes. He doesn't invite, he summons. He is the head. On the other hand, Mr. Stojic, well, does he summon General Praljak or does he invite him? That's what is at issue here. According to you, what's the score? Was it one of Stojic's powers to be able to summon or was it rather to invite Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would say that this is information about a meeting. Now, at the level of your questioning, I really cannot hazard a guess. I mustn't speculate. I know that the chief of the Main Staff is responsible to the president, that is why I don't dare hazard an answer to that question because I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger, I don't know whether that was helpful to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, but in the English interpretation the date the 1st of September appeared several times, but let me just say that the meeting was on the 2nd of September to avoid any subsequent problems if referring to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. You are quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: To get it correct, the invitation, however, is for the 1st. Invitation for the 1st September, I see, and it was actually then held on the 2nd.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but Judge Antonetti spoke about the minutes and on the minutes it says the 2nd of September, and that's what I wanted to draw your attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And sir, the final -- and I think this is the final topic that I would like to address with you, and now we are going to move to a time when you were dealing with personnel matters, and that was from July 1994. Is it correct that you were then the head of personnel administration in the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And could you perhaps just very briefly tell us what kind of things were you dealing with as the head of the personnel administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting, but in view of the time that this question refers to, that is to say a period outside the indictment, and in keeping with your instructions and guide-lines, perhaps my learned friend could explain to us why he is pursuing this line of questioning. It's irrelevant, as far as I'm concerned, but it's up to you to decide, but I would like my learned friend to explain why he is entering a period that goes beyond the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, when you yourself and General Praljak talk about Trusina, well, the OTP says the same thing, It's not in the indictment, we cannot refer to this. Now what is applied to you, must apply to him, so if he wishes to talk about 1994, he has a reason to do so. So let's wait and see what he wants to show.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and I think that it will become apparent very soon where this is going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, could you perhaps give the Court a very brief idea of what were your functions as head of the personnel administration, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mostly worked on reception and dealing with status issues and information and compiling files and records of people coming into the service, military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: So you would have had access also to all the personnel files of people who had previously been in the forces -- in the armed forces and who were currently at that stage in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that wasn't the type of information we received. In HZ-HB, and that territory, from the 1st of April, 1994, is when the pension system started functioning, and then everybody who was employed in the state services through set procedure, procedure that was prescribed, would send in their data, in personal data to the personnel administration and then they would take this up. And it was our task to deal with matters like health insurance, work booklet, the qualifications of the individuals, and so on. That kind of information is what we were interested in. Health insurance and so on. And there were several of us in the office that dealt with matters like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And if an inquiry came in that would entail going into the records of people who had previously served in the HVO, who would deal with such inquiries? Would it be your section?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the sector who was in the personnel administration in the hierarchy above, one level above.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. And who was that person, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was Mr. Matik Rasic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bruno Stojic, in 1995, was he also performing some function with regard to the ministry for personnel?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, at that time, but I'm not quite sure, it could have been the assistant for personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: There is documentation, I think, which refers to him as the assistant, and perhaps you could help us here, I don't know if it's the assistant minister for personnel or assistant to the minister of personnel. What, to your recollection, was he? Just an assistant to the minister for personnel?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, assistant. The deputy would be one chain, one link in the chain above.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Do you know what functions he performed as assistant?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The personnel administration had under it several sectors which were within a department, and at the head of that -- well, people who were in charge of the individual sectors for informatics, statistics, record keeping, and so on, they would see to that. They were purely administrative tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's have a look at the final exhibit, and that is P 10783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we go on to the last document, Witness, just a question, Mr. Stojic who had been minister for defence, this was an important position. And then later on, in 1995, he was deputy to the minister for defence; in other words, he was downgraded. Is that a normal procedure? Would that be a normal thing, as far as you know?
